---
title: "Data sources"
---

*Status: **v0.1 (provisional, milestone M2 in progress)**. This catalogue
is maintained alongside the machine-readable source list at
`data/catalogue/sources.yml`, which the acquisition pipeline reads. Every
URL below was verified reachable at the time of writing (see the
[data quality report](data-quality.qmd)).*

This is the project's inventory of the data that describe the state of
health in BC. **Data is construed broadly**: microdata, indicator tables,
dashboards, report figures, and catalogue/API discovery layers all
qualify, provided licence and governance checks pass. The aim is the best
use of all publicly available information that can be appropriately used
— not "microdata or nothing"
([roadmap](../ROADMAP.md), milestone M2).

## How to read an entry

Each source is catalogued with the following fields (see
`data/catalogue/sources.yml`):

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| **key** | stable identifier used by the pipeline |
| **form** | `microdata`, `indicator_table`, `dashboard`, `report_figure`, `api`, or `catalogue` (a discovery layer) |
| **domains** | which [measurement-framework](measurement-framework.qmd) domains it can serve |
| **resolution** | individual, neighbourhood, HSDA, LHA, health authority, provincial, international |
| **coverage** | the published time span of the series |
| **frequency / refresh** | how often observations are dated and how often the source is updated |
| **licence / access** | reuse terms and how you obtain it |
| **origin** | `bc`, `canada`, or `international` |
| **temporal behaviour** | expected behaviour: `trending`, `seasonal`, `shock_prone`, or `stable` |
| **quality notes** | suppressions, revisions, definitional breaks |

## Coverage of the measurement framework

Every domain in the [measurement framework](measurement-framework.qmd) is
served by at least one catalogued source:

| Domain | Catalogued sources |
|--------|--------------------|
| Mortality | Vital Statistics; BCCDC substance-use dashboard; BC overdose response; CIHI; Statistics Canada; FNHA |
| Physical morbidity | BCCDC data and reports; BCCDC chronic-disease dashboard; BC Cancer; CIHI; Statistics Canada; FNHA |
| Mental health | BCCDC substance-use dashboard; BCCDC data and reports; BC overdose response; CIHI; Statistics Canada; FNHA |
| Functional status | CIHI; Statistics Canada |
| Subjective wellbeing | Statistics Canada; FNHA |
| Social wellbeing | Statistics Canada; FNHA |

## Determinants and stratifiers

Used only to **stratify** health results, never as health outcomes
(see the [measurement framework](measurement-framework.qmd)):

| Source | Publisher | Provides | Resolution | Frequency |
|--------|-----------|----------|-----------|-----------|
| [Economy](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/data/statistics/economy) | BC Stats | income, employment, business counts | provincial, HA | annual |
| [People, Population and Community](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/data/statistics/people-population-community) | BC Stats | income, housing, families, migration | provincial → LHA | annual |
| [K-12 Reporting](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/education-training/k-12/administration/program-management/reporting-on-k-12) | Ministry of Education and Child Care | enrolment, completion, student outcomes | provincial, HA | annual |

## International and external-driver sources

| Source | Publisher | Form | Role | Resolution | Frequency |
|--------|-----------|------|------|-----------|-----------|
| [WHO data](https://www.who.int/data) | WHO | indicator tables | global reference, pandemic context | international | annual |
| [OECD Data Explorer](https://data-explorer.oecd.org/) | OECD | indicator tables | economic and health-system context | international | annual |
| [World Bank Open Data](https://data.worldbank.org/) | World Bank | indicator tables | macroeconomic context | international | annual |
| [Open Government](https://open.canada.ca/en/open-data) | Government of Canada | discovery | federal datasets reaching BC | provincial, international | continuous |

External drivers are catalogued with their **origin** and the mechanism by
which they reach BC in `data/catalogue/sources.yml` (`reaches_bc_via`):
for example, migration flows (`statcan_demography`), cross-border fire
and smoke (`cwfis`), and global pandemic conditions (`who_data`).

## Microdata access routes

Individual-level sources are catalogued as **access routes** — the
approval process, not the data:

| Source | Provider | Scope | Access |
|--------|----------|-------|--------|
| [Population Data BC](https://www.popdata.bc.ca/) | Population Data BC | BC administrative health records | application, ethics review, secure environment |
| [Microdata access](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/microdata/data-centres) | Statistics Canada | national survey microdata | Research Data Centres / remote access / custom tabulations |

These are catalogued even though the data cannot be committed: they set
the ceiling on what resolution is attainable and are the route to
individual-level indicators. **No individual-level data enters the
repository.**

## Governance and licences

- Licences vary by source and are recorded per entry. Check the record
  before redistributing anything.
- No individual-level data is stored in the repository. Only
  aggregate/public sources are fetched, and fetched data are
  reproducible artefacts (`data/raw/`) that are never committed.
- First Nations data are governed by First Nations principles and
  specific agreements; reuse must respect [@fnigcOcap].

## Reproducing the catalogue

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=src
python3 -m sohbc validate   # schema check
python3 -m sohbc list       # list sources
python3 -m sohbc check --all --include-download   # re-verify URLs
python3 -m sohbc fetch --all
```

See [How to ingest a data source](../how-to/ingest-data.qmd).
